summary:
Our project, Space Mission Design Game, is an interactive educational game developed using Godot to make the complex process of space mission planning easier to understand and more engaging. Players take on the role of mission designers, making decisions about science objectives, spacecraft, scientific instruments, launch vehicles, and orbits while balancing important constraints such as mass, power, budget, communications, and mission lifetime.

The project addresses the challenge by transforming traditional mission design concepts into a hands-on experience where players can explore the consequences of their decisions, experiment with different configurations, and learn through trial and error. We aim to make space mission planning more accessible, engaging, and collaborative, helping students and space enthusiasts understand the engineering and scientific trade-offs behind real NASA missions.

Ultimately, our goal is to inspire curiosity about space exploration and encourage the next generation to think like mission designers.
details:
Project Details – Space Mission Design Game

Our project, Space Mission Design Game, is an interactive educational game designed to introduce players to the challenges of planning and designing space missions. Developed using Godot, the game allows players to experience the role of a space mission designer by making decisions that influence the success of a mission.

How It Works

Players begin by selecting a scientific objective for their mission. They then make important design decisions, including choosing a spacecraft, scientific instruments, launch vehicle, and orbit. Throughout the process, they must consider and balance different mission constraints, such as mass, power consumption, budget, communication capabilities, and mission lifetime. The game aims to evaluate mission configurations and demonstrate how each decision can affect the final outcome.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes complex aerospace engineering concepts easier to understand through practical interaction rather than theory alone. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and teamwork. Our intended impact is to make space exploration and mission engineering more accessible to students and space enthusiasts, while inspiring interest in STEM fields.

Tools and Technologies

The main development platform is Godot, with C# used for game programming. We also aim to incorporate relevant NASA open data, mission information, and educational resources to make the game scenarios more realistic and informative.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of our project is turning the complex process of space mission design into an interactive game. Instead of simply reading about spacecraft and mission requirements, players can experiment with different configurations, discover trade-offs, and learn from the results of their decisions.

Factors Considered

Our team considered scientific objectives, engineering limitations, resource management, mission feasibility, educational value, and user experience. We also considered how to make the experience understandable for beginners while still presenting meaningful challenges. Our goal is to combine learning, creativity, and the excitement of space exploration in one engaging experience.
